# OpenShell Dashboard Helm chart

<!-- Generated by helm-docs; edit README.md.gotmpl and values.yaml, then run `make helm-docs` -->

Deploys one stateless dashboard Deployment alongside an [OpenShell gateway](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/tree/main/deploy/helm/openshell). Only the oauth2-proxy sidecar is exposed. The BFF binds `127.0.0.1:8080`; the Service and NetworkPolicy expose only proxy port 4180. The chart creates no certificates for the gateway, no database and no cluster RBAC.

## Install

**Prerequisites:**

- A running OpenShell gateway of the dashboard's release line, installed as release `openshell`. The dashboard goes into the same namespace, because the chart mounts the gateway's CA from the Secret `openshell-client-tls` there.
- A confidential OIDC client for oauth2-proxy at the issuer the gateway trusts, with the callback `https://<dashboard host>/oauth2/callback`.
- A Secret with that client's secret and a cookie secret. The chart does not create it:

```sh
kubectl -n openshell create secret generic openshell-dashboard-oidc \
  --from-literal=client-secret='<client secret of the openshell-dashboard client>' \
  --from-literal=cookie-secret="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
```

A `values.yaml` for Keycloak and an existing Gateway:

```yaml
oidc:
  provider: keycloak-oidc
  issuer: https://keycloak.example.com/realms/openshell
  codeChallengeMethod: S256
  adminRole: openshell-admin
  allowedRoles:
    - openshell-api:openshell-admin
    - openshell-api:openshell-user

httpRoute:
  enabled: true
  hostnames: [dashboard.example.com]
  gateway:
    name: <your Gateway>
    namespace: <its namespace>
    sectionName: <name of its HTTPS listener>

networkPolicy:
  ingressNamespace: <namespace of the Gateway's data-plane pods>
```

Install the published chart:

```sh
helm upgrade --install openshell-dashboard \
  oci://ghcr.io/gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/helm-chart/openshell-dashboard \
  --version <dashboard version> --namespace openshell -f values.yaml
```

`<dashboard version>` is the newest dashboard release whose first two numbers match your gateway's: a `0.1.N` for a gateway `0.1.x` ([Compatibility](https://github.com/Gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard#compatibility), [releases](https://github.com/Gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/releases)).

The [install guide](https://github.com/Gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/blob/main/docs/install.md) has every step: the Keycloak realm, the gateway's settings, OpenShift, sign-out and workspace membership.

## Configuration notes

- **Identity provider**
  - `oidc.provider` is `oidc` for any OIDC issuer and `keycloak-oidc` for Keycloak. Limit who reaches the UI with `oidc.allowedRoles`, which needs `keycloak-oidc`, or with `oidc.allowedGroups`.
  - `oidc.clientIdSecretKey` takes the client ID from the Secret and wins over `oidc.clientId`. `oidc.caConfigMapName` trusts an issuer certificate from a private CA.
  - oauth2-proxy forwards the access token. The gateway's issuer, audience, roles claim, admin role and user role have to agree with what that token carries; the [install guide](https://github.com/Gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the gateway's key names.
  - `oidc.audience` and `oidc.rolesClaim` are informational: they change no token, and the chart only prints the audience in its post-install notes.
- **Gateway connection**
  - The chart mounts the gateway's CA from the Secret `gateway.caSecretName`, key `gateway.caKey`, in the release namespace.
  - `gateway.url` takes `grpcs://` or `https://` for TLS and `grpc://` or `http://` for plaintext. Left empty, it is built from `gateway.serviceName` and the release namespace.
  - `gateway.clientCertSecretName` is for a gateway that requires a client certificate and has no OIDC. Every signed-in user then reaches the gateway as that one certificate, so the chart requires `oidc.allowedGroups` or `oidc.allowedRoles` with it.
  - For a gateway without TLS, set `gateway.tls.enabled: false` and empty `gateway.caSecretName`. Browsers still need HTTPS.
- **Exposure and NetworkPolicy**
  - `openshiftRoute` creates an edge or reencrypt Route and `httpRoute` a Gateway API HTTPRoute. There is no Ingress template.
  - On an existing Gateway, set `httpRoute.gateway.sectionName` to the HTTPS listener, and make sure the Gateway admits routes from the release namespace.
  - The NetworkPolicy admits the proxy port from one namespace: `openshift-ingress`, or with an HTTPRoute the Gateway's namespace. Set `networkPolicy.ingressNamespace` to where the ingress data-plane pods run, or `networkPolicy.ingressFrom` for other peers.
  - Whatever is in front has to keep the Host header, pass WebSocket upgrades and leave a terminal's connection open. The Route's timeouts are set (300s, and 1h for WebSockets); the HTTPRoute sets none.
  - Never expose pod port 8080: the BFF behind it does not authenticate anyone.
- **Versions and images**
  - The chart version is the dashboard image version, and a published version is never replaced. A checkout of the chart is version `0.0.0`, for which there is no image.
  - Pin an image with `dashboard.image.digest` or `authProxy.image.digest`. For a registry mirror, set `global.image.registry` and each `repository`.
  - The dashboard's probes run `probes.*.dashboardCommand`; the default is the binary's own `--healthcheck`.

## Values
## Values

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| affinity | object | `{}` | Affinity. |
| authProxy.apiRoutes | list | `["^/api/"]` | API path patterns that return HTTP 401 instead of redirecting to the identity provider on an expired session. |
| authProxy.cookie.name | string | `"_oauth2_proxy"` | Session cookie name; use a distinct name when dashboards share a hostname. |
| authProxy.cookie.refresh | string | `"2m"` | Interval for refreshing the access token; set below the issuer's access-token lifetime. Empty disables refresh. |
| authProxy.cookie.sameSite | string | `"lax"` | Session cookie SameSite attribute (lax, strict, none, or empty to omit). |
| authProxy.extraArgs | list | `[]` | Additional oauth2-proxy flags, appended after chart-generated arguments. |
| authProxy.forceHTTPS | bool | `false` | Force HTTP requests to HTTPS at the proxy. Requires authProxy.tls.secretName; leave false behind TLS-terminating ingress. |
| authProxy.image.digest | string | `""` | Proxy image digest; takes precedence over tag. |
| authProxy.image.pullPolicy | string | `nil` | Proxy pull policy; null uses global.image.pullPolicy. |
| authProxy.image.registry | string | `""` | oauth2-proxy registry; empty uses global.image.registry. |
| authProxy.image.repository | string | `"oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy"` | oauth2-proxy repository. Change it to pull the proxy from another registry or a mirror. |
| authProxy.image.tag | string | `"v7.15.2"` | oauth2-proxy image tag. |
| authProxy.port | int | `4180` | Port on which oauth2-proxy listens. |
| authProxy.resources | object | `{}` | Resource requests/limits for oauth2-proxy. |
| authProxy.tls.secretName | string | `""` | Secret with tls.crt/tls.key for HTTPS proxy backend (required for Route reencrypt). |
| authProxy.upstreamTimeout | string | `"120s"` | Maximum amount of time the proxy will wait for a response from the upstream. |
| authProxy.whitelistDomains | list | `[]` | Allowed redirect domains (including IdP sign-out redirects); prefix with . or *. to allow subdomains. Setting the list also drops the `skip-provider-button` flag, which authProxy.extraArgs can add back. |
| autoscaling.enabled | bool | `false` | Create autoscaling/v2 HPA (CPU/memory metrics need requests or limits on both containers). |
| autoscaling.maxReplicas | int | `4` | Maximum replicas. |
| autoscaling.minReplicas | int | `1` | Minimum replicas. |
| autoscaling.targetCPUUtilizationPercentage | int | `80` | CPU target utilization (null to disable). |
| autoscaling.targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage | string | `nil` | Memory target utilization (null to disable). |
| dashboard.image.digest | string | `""` | Dashboard image digest; takes precedence over tag. |
| dashboard.image.pullPolicy | string | `nil` | Dashboard pull policy; null uses global.image.pullPolicy. |
| dashboard.image.registry | string | `""` | Dashboard image registry; empty uses global.image.registry. |
| dashboard.image.repository | string | `"gkrumbach07/openshell-dashboard"` | Dashboard image repository. |
| dashboard.image.tag | string | `""` | Dashboard image tag; empty uses global.image.tag then Chart.appVersion. |
| dashboard.logoutURL | string | `"/oauth2/sign_out?rd=/oauth2/sign_in"` | Browser-facing sign-out URL; rd returns to oauth2-proxy sign-in after clearing the session. |
| dashboard.port | int | `8080` | Dashboard container port (loopback only; never exposed via Service). |
| fullnameOverride | string | `""` | Full resource name override. |
| gateway.caKey | string | `"ca.crt"` | CA key in the Secret. |
| gateway.caSecretName | string | `"openshell-client-tls"` | TLS CA Secret in the release namespace. Empty only with a plaintext grpc:// or http:// gateway URL. |
| gateway.clientCertSecretName | string | `""` | Optional client cert Secret (tls.crt/tls.key), for mTLS-only gateways. With OIDC, the forwarded bearer token alone suffices. |
| gateway.preflight.enabled | bool | `false` | Check gateway Service exists via lookup (requires live cluster; disable for offline rendering). |
| gateway.serviceName | string | `"openshell"` | Name of the OpenShell gateway's Service: openshell when the gateway is installed as release openshell. |
| gateway.tls.enabled | bool | `true` | Use grpcs:// for the derived gateway URL; disable only with gateway.caSecretName empty. |
| gateway.url | string | `""` | Gateway gRPC URL (grpcs:// or https:// for TLS; grpc:// or http:// for plaintext). Empty derives scheme from gateway.tls.enabled and uses <serviceName>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8080. |
| global.image.pullPolicy | string | `"IfNotPresent"` | Shared image pull policy. |
| global.image.registry | string | `"quay.io"` | Shared image registry; per-component registry overrides it. |
| global.image.tag | string | `""` | Shared image tag; defaults to Chart.appVersion when empty. |
| httpRoute.annotations | object | `{}` | HTTPRoute annotations. |
| httpRoute.enabled | bool | `false` | Create a Gateway API HTTPRoute to the proxy Service. |
| httpRoute.gateway.className | string | `"eg"` | GatewayClass for created Gateway. |
| httpRoute.gateway.create | bool | `false` | Create a Gateway in the release namespace; else use an existing one. |
| httpRoute.gateway.listener.allowedRoutes | string | `"Same"` | Allowed route namespaces: Same or All. |
| httpRoute.gateway.listener.port | int | `443` | Listener port. |
| httpRoute.gateway.listener.protocol | string | `"HTTPS"` | Listener protocol: HTTPS (recommended) or HTTP behind a separate trusted TLS terminator. |

| httpRoute.gateway.sectionName | string | `""` | Listener name when attaching to an existing Gateway. Set it to the HTTPS listener: without it the route attaches to every listener that admits it. For a Gateway this chart creates, the chart sets it. |
| httpRoute.hostnames | list | `[]` | Public hostnames; first hostname supplies callback URL if redirectURL is empty. |
| imagePullSecrets | list | `[]` | Image pull secrets for the dashboard pod. |
| nameOverride | string | `"openshell-dashboard"` | Resource name override; pod identity label remains openshell-dashboard. |
| networkPolicy.enabled | bool | `true` | Restrict ingress to the proxy port from the ingress controller namespace. |
| networkPolicy.ingressFrom | list | `[]` | Optional ingress peers replacing the default namespace selector (e.g. host-network routers or Gateway data-plane pods). |
| networkPolicy.ingressNamespace | string | `""` | Namespace of ingress data-plane pods. Defaults to openshift-ingress for Routes; required for HTTPRoute unless ingressFrom is set. |
| nodeSelector | object | `{}` | Node selector. |
| oidc.adminRole | string | `""` | Role name for admin access. Must be the same as the openshell gateway admin name. Defaults to "admin" |
| oidc.allowedGroups | list | `[]` | Allowed groups for generic OIDC or other providers; empty allows any authenticated user. |
| oidc.allowedRoles | list | `[]` | Allowed Keycloak roles (realm role or client:role); requires provider=keycloak-oidc. Multiple roles are alternatives. |
| oidc.audience | string | `"openshell-api"` | Expected audience claim for the API resource server. IdP must add it to token aud. Purely informational: the chart only prints it in the post-install notes. |
| oidc.backendLogoutURL | string | `"auto"` | IdP logout URL oauth2-proxy calls from the pod when a user signs out (HTTP GET), so the IdP session ends too; {id_token} is replaced with the session ID token. `auto` derives it from the issuer for provider keycloak-oidc (`<issuer>/protocol/openid-connect/logout?id_token_hint={id_token}`) and sets none for other providers. Empty disables backend logout. Separate from dashboard.logoutURL. |
| oidc.caConfigMapName | string | `""` | ConfigMap with ca.crt to trust private issuer TLS (also set on gateway). |
| oidc.clientId | string | `"openshell-dashboard"` | OAuth2-proxy OIDC client ID. |
| oidc.clientIdSecretKey | string | `""` | Optional key in oidc.existingSecret holding client ID; when set, takes precedence over oidc.clientId. |
| oidc.codeChallengeMethod | string | `""` | PKCE challenge method (e.g. S256); empty disables PKCE for providers that do not support it. |
| oidc.existingSecret | string | `"openshell-dashboard-oidc"` | Existing Secret containing keys client-secret and cookie-secret. |
| oidc.issuer | string | `""` | OIDC issuer URL (e.g. https://keycloak.example.com/realms/openshell) |
| oidc.provider | string | `"oidc"` | oauth2-proxy provider (oidc for generic OIDC, keycloak-oidc for Keycloak role filtering). |
| oidc.redirectURL | string | `""` | Full public callback URL; required when host is dynamically allocated. Empty derives from Route/HTTPRoute host. |
| oidc.rolesClaim | string | `""` | Roles claim path, the same as the gateway's roles claim. Informational: the chart does not read it. |
| oidc.scope | string | `""` | OAuth2 scopes; empty uses the provider default (openid email profile for generic OIDC). |
| openshiftRoute.annotations | object | `{"haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout":"300s","haproxy.router.openshift.io/timeout-tunnel":"1h"}` | Route annotations; the timeouts cover long-lived terminal WebSockets. |
| openshiftRoute.destinationCACertificate | string | `""` | CA PEM for reencrypt backend validation (requires a separate TLS-enabled proxy configuration). |
| openshiftRoute.enabled | bool | `false` | Create an edge/reencrypt OpenShift Route (never passthrough). |
| openshiftRoute.host | string | `""` | Public Route hostname; required unless oidc.redirectURL is set explicitly. |
| openshiftRoute.termination | string | `"edge"` | TLS termination at router: edge or reencrypt. Reencrypt requires proxy TLS and destination CA below. |
| podAnnotations | object | `{}` | Extra pod annotations. |
| podLabels | object | `{}` | Extra pod labels; cannot override identity/instance selector labels. |
| podLifecycle.terminationGracePeriodSeconds | int | `30` | Pod termination grace period in seconds. |
| podSecurityContext.fsGroup | int | `1000` | fsGroup of the pod; on OpenShift set podSecurityContext to null. |
| probes.liveness.dashboardCommand | list | `["/usr/local/bin/openshell-dashboard","--healthcheck"]` | Dashboard exec command for liveness. |
| probes.liveness.failureThreshold | int | `3` | Liveness probe failure threshold. |
| probes.liveness.periodSeconds | int | `10` | Liveness probe period in seconds. |

| probes.readiness.periodSeconds | int | `5` | Readiness probe period in seconds. |
